# Monte Carlo Simulations {#sec-mc}

Real data never tell us the truth. We do not know the true parameter, and we do not know whether the assumptions of our method hold. In a Monte Carlo simulation, *we* choose the data generating process, so we know the truth, and we can watch how a method behaves when its assumptions hold and when they break.

This makes Monte Carlo simulations the main tool of this seminar. Before you study your own method, we learn together how to build Monte Carlo simulations in the first meetings of the seminar. Afterwards, you will use them in your seminar thesis to investigate when your method works and when it fails (see @sec-thesis).

## Material

In our first meetings, we work with the Monte Carlo chapter of my coding intros. They cover random samples, data generating processes, and how to check 

:::{.spaced-list}
* Unbiasedness 
* Consistency 
* Asymptotic normality, and 
* Size & Power of statistical tests and confidence intervals 
:::
